shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling/needs/work/storage come free from vanilla. Levels and per-level size are bought from a 146,000-cell budget; colder with altitude, richer ore and more cave with depth. Multi-level rendering, interaction and group ordering all verified in play.
body:
# As above, So below II — V2

> V1 is **DELETED**. ~59 files / ~15,400 LOC.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount × Slot)`; bands along **+z** from the deepest basement; permanently-fogged gutter between bands; `Slot = ceil((bandHeight+2)/64)×64` — **64-alignment is load-bearing**. Per-level sizes 126 / 190 / 254, each just under a 64 boundary (~1-2% gutter waste).

### The one insight
`Region.Neighbors` is **topological, not spatial**. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms/temperature/vacuum; `Reachability.CanReach` works **unpatched**. **But reachability ≠ a path** — 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

### Hard 1.6 constraints
Path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell ⇒ **total stacked cells is the runtime metric** · no `PathFinder.FindPath` · `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

# 2. LEVEL PLAN — cell budget = **146,000**
Player buys level COUNT and per-level DIMENSION from one budget on the advanced-config screen. `4 × 190 = 145,920` is what sets the figure; `2 × 254 = 130,048`, `7 × 126 = 112,896`; `5 × 190 = 182,400` and `7 × 190 = 255,360` refused (3-up-and-3-down at 190 auto-drops the size to 126 — the intended trade).
`ABMapSizeLimit` owns it: `UpperLevels`/`LowerLevels` (0-3 each), `BandCount`, `SurfaceBand = lower`, `Fits`, `MaxSize`, `MaxLevelsFor`, `StackedCells`. `ABV2.BandCount`/`SurfaceBand` are properties (were consts — the only thing pinning the mod to 3 levels).

### ⚠ THE CHOOSER UI — own the widget, don't patch the data
**`Dialog_AdvancedGameConfig.MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap of it SILENTLY FAILED in play.** Proof from a screenshot: vanilla's Small/Medium/Large group headers only render for sizes 200/250/300, so their presence meant our array was never in use. Worse, the postfix then re-snapped `GameInitData.mapSize` **every frame**, undoing every click — reported as "map sizes don't show correctly and nothing is selected".
**Now:** our own radio buttons live in our strip and write `mapSize` directly (a click sticks); every vanilla size is locked outright so there is exactly one control; the strip also shows cells-used-vs-budget and "this size affords up to N levels". Window grown +260px tall / ≥1000 wide via an `InitialSize` postfix — **vanilla lays its columns from the top and never consults the height, so added space is ours; never guess at free space inside another mod's dialog.**

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix → tick sweep carries the pawn → `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` **BFSes the band graph** and returns the best pair whose far band is `hops-1` from the target; chaining is free because each leg re-plans, and hops must strictly decrease or pawns ping-pong.
**Caveat:** an intermediate level must be walkable between arrival and the next staircase; sky levels are mostly impassable open air, so stacked stair towers work and scattered flights strand a pawn. **STILL UNTESTED IN PLAY — no test map has ever had a stair tower built.**

# 4. GROUP ORDERING — three wrong layers before the right one
1. `FloatMenuMakerMap.GetOptions` clickPos — **wrong layer**; grouped orders never touch it.
2. Per-pawn `RCellFinder.BestOrderedGotoDestNear` prefix — fixed single orders but **fought vanilla's formation**.
3. **Correct:** `RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection ALONG the drag line (`root = start + (end-start) * j/(count-1)`). With endpoints on different bands that line runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature the user spotted ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 don't") is the proof: only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5, and the midpoint of a one-Slot drag is the impassable gutter. Fix = normalise `start`/`end` into the commanded pawns' band, leaving vanilla's maths untouched. **Verified fixed.**
Also: ordering never translates across bands unless `CanReach` says a route exists; same-level orders snap to nearest ground within radius 8; the `BestOrderedGotoDestNear` prefix survives as a safety net for crates/hackables/single moves.
`MultiPawnGotoController.Draw` is re-emitted with positions lifted into the view band. Falls through to vanilla on any missing member or throw.

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE — `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor or the bottom band, returns the accumulated `drop`. **NINE systems share it:** `SectionLayer_ABBelowV2`, `ABBelowClickThrough`, `ABBelowOverlays`, `ABBelowDynamicDraw`, `ABBelowSelectionDraw`, `ABBelowMultiSelect`, `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen`, and — since the visuality pass — **`SectionLayer_ABBelowShadows` and `SectionLayer_ABBelowEdgeShadows`**.
A single `- Slot` step works on a 3-level map and breaks the instant two see-through levels stack. **This same bug has now appeared SEVEN times.** Appearances #6/#7 were the shadow layers, reported as *"shadows show on the first upper level, but not on upper 2 or 3"*: from +1 the single step lands on the opaque surface and works; from +2/+3 it lands in the OPEN AIR of the level between, which holds no edifices, so nothing casts.
**Sun-shadow subtlety:** that layer's mask is deliberately *neighbour*-based (a mountain-edge caster sits under an opaque cap and can never resolve a descent of its own), so mask and descent are now answered together by `TryResolveDropAround`, which takes the **smallest** drop among the nine cells — the highest visible floor, i.e. the surface most of the surrounding view is showing. **FIX BUILT, NOT YET CONFIRMED IN PLAY.**
**Still single-band:** the realtime-things pass in `ABBelowDynamicDraw` (motes, fire).
Also: the **dirty mirror** invalidates EVERY band above, not one.

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION — verified in play
**⚠ FOUR REJECTED ATTEMPTS — do not revisit:** force-linked wall masks · high-queue cover · wall-sprite suppression · theorising twice about "flat" mountains before running the below-layer report.
Vanilla sprites always draw; redundant outlines are a GENERATION problem. Despeckle (majority filter; **wall dissolves only at 7+ open neighbours** — at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge) · one central fog hole · five-terrain plateau palette · cliff faces (`CliffFaceDepth 2`, `FaceDarkest 0.42`) · alpine pass (shallow-only tarns with a per-cell 6-cell edge rule, rim scree via `"Chunk"+defName`, exposure-thinned flora).
**Cross-band decoration:** `EmitMassSilhouetteAt` + static `EmitMeadowFadeAt` emit lip, corner fillers, cliff shading and meadow fades into ANY layer at a z offset. Diagnosed from a below-layer report showing **no edge material at all** — nothing failed to print; the decoration lived in the other band's mesh.
**Ore glyph bug:** ore defs have no `naturalTerrain` (`TerrainDefGenerator_Stone` skips `isResourceRock`) ⇒ a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole **atlas sheet** per cell. `IsHostStone()` gate + fallback deleted.

# 6b. ⚠ WATER — `ABWaterV2.cs`. **1.6 water is a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect**
The single fact behind most water bugs: `SectionLayer_Watergen` renders `TerrainDef.waterDepthMaterial` into the **WaterDepth SUBCAMERA's** render texture (its own Unity layer, not the map mesh), and the visible `Map/TerrainWater` material samples that (`_WaterOutputTex`) **at its own screen position**. Water is not self-contained geometry — printing the water material where the depth pass never wrote yields **nothing at all**.

- **Water vanished from any upper level.** Half of a two-pass effect was missing. Fixed by `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` — mirrors vanilla's `internal` Watergen (`waterDepthMaterial` + water-to-water edge fans for shoreline gradients), descends via `TryResolveVisibleBelow`, and **overrides `DrawLayer` to target `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`**. Bisect toggle: *below water depth*. **BUILT, NOT YET CONFIRMED IN PLAY.**
- **Rivers "did not generate" — VERIFIED FIXED.** They generated perfectly, three levels up. `TileMutatorWorker_River.GetRiverCenter` picks `Rand.Range(0.3f,0.7f) × map.Size.z`, a fraction of the whole STACK. Remapped into the surface band preserving the *roll*, not the absolute z. Patched on `GetRiverCenter`, **not** `Init`, because Init consumes the centre immediately to build bend noise and edge nodes; the delta/confluence/headwater/island variants inherit it, so one patch covers the family. **`TileMutatorWorker_Lake.GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first one** — `River.Init` *prefers* an existing `waterInfo.lakeCenter` over its own roll. (Lake path still untested — no lake tile has been rolled yet.)
  Proof from the water report on a 4×190 map: node `start=(-25,0,155.9) end=(215,0,33.5)`, `band 0 baseRiver=3079`, every other band `0`.
- **Why the band square makes this work:** the band is 190×190 out of 190×768, so a line through a re-anchored centre crosses it exactly as it would cross an ordinary map, and the bend noise peaks at the segment midpoint = the anchor.
- **⚠ REJECTED — DO NOT RETRY: republishing `_MapSize` as one band.** Theory: `WaterInfo.SetTextures` publishes `_MapSize` as the whole stack, so anything UV'd by `worldPos.xz / _MapSize` smears bandCount-times north-south — which fitted "water always goes vertical, even in lakes" perfectly, *including its uniformity*. Shipped behind an A/B toggle and **DISPROVED IN ONE LAUNCH**: banding the global is what MAKES water run north-south; vanilla's full-stack value looks correct. The measurement was airtight because `surfaceBand=0` on the test map, so the band fold was the IDENTITY and both addressings hit the same texture row — flow data was bit-identical, leaving `_MapSize.y` as the only variable. The band-folded REPEAT-wrapped flow texture went with it (vanilla's full-height texture is already 1:1 correct for every band, since rivers only live on the surface). The report still prints `_MapSize` so this stays disproved instead of getting re-theorised.
- **OPEN: what actually caused "lakes flow north-south".** Leading theory is the **ghost river** — pre-fix, a river generated into a sky band was carved away but `riverFlowMap` was still computed from it, leaving a degenerate field for surviving water to sample. If so, the anchoring fix closes it as a side effect. **Discriminator, costs nothing:** the sky **tarns** (shallow *still* water, 137/89/32 cells on bands 1/2/3 of the 4×190 map) have zero flow exactly like a lake. Calm tarn ⇒ ghost river was it. Flowing tarn ⇒ separate live bug, fix by not shipping a degenerate flow field for still water.

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Sky temp `-4°C × level` (compounds) · basement flat -6 · ore `×(1+0.45×(depth-1))`, cave openness `×(1+0.35×(depth-1))`, both AFTER the settings clamp so the slider is the level-1 baseline · mountains taper upward for free.
**Snow line:** generation-time snow seeding **REMOVED** (user call — a pre-frozen top level made the most expensive level read as a different biome instead of higher ground). Nothing lost: vanilla accumulates/melts snow per-CELL temperature and the per-level offset already makes high levels cold, so high ground still collects real snowfall, holds it after the surface thaws, and the line moves seasonally — earned, not painted on at t=0.

# 8. CAMERA
`freeCameraPan` REMOVED. `ABCameraBounds.For(level)` keyed by **level**, calibrated on a 126 band: `panMargin 63.5` for +1/+3, **`maxZoom` left DERIVED** (measured 60.0 was just where the camera stopped; derive is 63.0 and an absolute would mis-scale a 190 band, where derive is 95). `Dialog_ABCameraCalibration` opens with the clamp UNLOCKED — **a calibration tool must suspend the limit it calibrates.** Clamp bails while `Scribe` is active or state isn't `Playing`.

# 9. ⚠ GENERATION COST — the top open item
| Config | Cells | Carve | Things destroyed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 × 190 | 109,440 | 5.0 s | 14,971 |
| 4 × 126 | 64,512 | 3.0 s | 24,490 |
| 7 × 126 | 112,896 | 30.4 s | 62,686 |
| 4 × 190 (earlier) | 145,920 | 20.4 s | 79,706 |
| **4 × 190 (run #167, river tile)** | **145,920** | **18.7 s** | **56,318** |
**`Sky clear` is ~97% of the carve**, and **`0 rocks spawned`**: every destroyed thing is vanilla content generated into doomed sky bands and immediately deleted. Superlinear in thing count, because `ListerThings.Remove` is linear.
**NEW from run #167:** band 1's sky clear was **11.1 s vs 3.6/3.5 s for bands 2-3** — the first sky band is ~3× the others, so doomed-band scoping should pay off most there. Also `MutatorPostTerrain` was the biggest genstep at **3646 ms** (river `GeneratePostTerrain`: a 240×818 depth map per node + two `GetDepth` calls per cell).
**THE FIX — extend the doomed-band genstep skip.** Precedent: `Patch_WildPlantSpawner_ABSkipDoomedBands` took generation 16.9 s → 4.2 s. Targets: `RocksFromGrid` (751 ms), `Terrain`, `RockChunks`, `ScatterRuinsSimple`, `CaveHives`, `MutatorPostElevationFertility`, `Plants`.
**HARD CONSTRAINT: per-cell gensteps scope safely; `map.Area`-count scatterers do NOT** — they would dump their whole quota into the surface band. Audit `ScatterShrines`/`ScatterRuinsSimple` individually.
**Do not blanket-skip the water mutators** — §6b depends on them running, just anchored correctly.

# 10. RUNTIME PERF — 59.6 fps @96 pawns, mod ≈2% frame. All rendering is bake-time section-mesh geometry.

# 11. VERTICAL LINKS — elevator SHIPPED, **untested**. Full-mesh 2×2; mesh is O(n²) in band count. Known: `Carry` latent hole.

# 12. DIAGNOSTICS
band info · **below layer report** (submesh dump — use it BEFORE theorising) · below pawn report · **water report** (per-band water/withDepthMat/baseRiver census + riverGraph + flow map + published `_MapSize` — it is what proved the river now lands in band 0) · transit health · stuck probe · transit logging · lighting/shader/biome reports · bisect toggles (click-through, below multi-select, below terrain/things/air-mask/lighting, **below water depth**) · ABGenProfile · camera calibration · `CliffFaceDepth`.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **Confirm the un-verified half of the visuality pass:** shadows on +2/+3, the below-water depth pass, and the tarn discriminator for §6b's open question. All three are one walk up the levels.
2. **Doomed-band genstep scoping pass** (§9) — biggest remaining win; band 1 first.
3. **Compat, specced, not yet written:**
   - **Map Preview** (`m00nl1ght.MapPreview`) — never sees our banding: `MapPreviewRequest` runs only `ElevationFertility`/`Terrain`/`MutatorPost*` on its own map, **never through `MapGenerator.GenerateMap`**, sized from `world.info.initialMapSize` which we deliberately keep at the SURFACE size. So it previews a normal square map while the real surface band is a horizontal slice of a much taller one — different noise entirely. Fix = generate at the inflated height, crop the texture to the surface band. Must be **reflection-only** (Lunar component, dynamically loaded). Hooks: `MapPreviewAPI.IsGeneratingPreview`, `MapSizeUtility.MapSizeOverride`, `MapPreviewRequest.TextureSize`.
   - **Dubs Mint Minimap** (`dubwise.dubsmintminimap`) — should show only the active level. Fully patchable, ~250 LOC: everything keys off `map.Size` and one static `MapTexture`; band-scoping needs `UpdateMapTex` **plus** the coordinate mapping in `Minimap`/`DrawAllPawns`/`DrawFires`/`DrawProjectiles`/`DrawPings`/`DrawCam`, all lerping against `map.Size.z`. It also draws the tall texture through `DrawTextureFitted(..., texProportions: 1f)`, so today the whole stack is squashed into a square.
4. **Never exercised in play:** multi-hop stair router (needs a stair tower), elevator, reload fix, lake-anchor patch (no lake tile rolled yet).
5. Realtime-things pass still single-band (motes/fire >1 level down).
6. Selection bracket **drifts upward as you zoom out** — zoom-dependence means that path mixes world and screen space; our offset is in world units.
7. **Option E — waterfalls**: de-risked once the below-water depth pass is confirmed.
8. COMBAT never verified · Option C (stepped mesa) parked · vertical conduit · compat audit incl. Better Mountains · transplant (coastline slicing — **river slicing is fixed by anchoring**) · **store page still says three levels**.

# 14. LESSONS (telegraphic)
**Run the diagnostic before the third theory** · **build the A/B discriminator INTO any change whose mechanism you cannot read** — the `_MapSize` theory fitted every symptom including its uniformity and was still WRONG; the toggle cost one launch instead of a release · **a beautiful fit is not evidence** · **an odd/even or count-dependent symptom is arithmetic — find the formula** · **a UNIFORM symptom is a scale/constant, a PATCHY one is data** (right instinct, wrong constant) · **when a symptom says "X is missing", ask how many PASSES X takes** — 1.6 water is two, and only one was ported · measure, don't extrapolate · **a single-step assumption survives until the data has two steps — grep `X + 1`, `== N`, every `- Slot`; it has now bitten SEVEN times** · **generation anchors picked as a fraction of `map.Size.z` all land in the wrong band — audit every one** · **patch the method that PRODUCES a value, not the one that stores it, when the storer consumes it immediately** · **own the widget instead of patching the data it reads; `static readonly` reflection writes fail silently** · **never fight the player's input every frame** · never hide sprites that carry gameplay information · visual noise in generated content is a GENERATION bug · ore defs have no naturalTerrain · a `Graphic_Linked` base material is the whole ATLAS SHEET · **"can't happen" fallbacks are what the player photographs** · enforce spatial rules PER CELL, not seed+radius · key authored tables by stable semantics (level), not index · **budget the real cost, don't cap a proxy** · a per-leg re-planning router needs only the FIRST HOP of a BFS · **normalise the anchor, don't rewrite each member** · never a queue-above-cutout cover · clip geometry to cells you own · vertex colour on terrain dims the real texture · statics keyed by game-scoped ids leak — CWT · **Unity textures are not GC'd with their owner** · never cache comps while Scribe active · FinalizeInit = worker thread · altitude ≠ draw order but IS the cutout depth tiebreaker · `material.shader =` resets renderQueue · static Unity-asset fields need `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]` · `SectionLayer` subclasses are **auto-discovered** by `Section`'s ctor — no registration · when art is in asset bundles, playtest screenshots are a legitimate mockup source.

## TESTING RULE
`isolated=true`. Companions: `astryl.Circinus` + `astryl.ModernDevTools` + `BiomesTeam.BiomesCaverns` + `BiomesTeam.CoreFramework` — **drop them when a bug might not be ours** (that discriminator proved the group-order bug WAS ours; run #167 ran clean with none). Multi-level tests need `quicktest=false`. Reload tests need load-while-playing. **Water/river tests need a tile that actually has a river or lake landmark** — pick one deliberately on the world map, and take a fresh colony (anchoring is generation-time only). **A `surfaceBand=0` config cannot test band-folded addressing** — use lower levels for that.
